judged_text: updateEvent's fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` only executes when externalCalendarId is falsy, so it searches for a calendar whose externalId equals undefined, never matches, and makes selectedCalendar always undefined in that branch — the old code fell back to event.destinationCalendar?.externalId. adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` `updateEvent()`, the fallback branch now computes `selectedCalendar` as `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` only when `externalCalendarId` is falsy. In that case `externalCalendarId` is `undefined/null`, so the `.find(...)` searches for a calendar whose `externalId` equals `undefined`, which will almost never match, leaving `selectedCalendar` undefined. The old code fell back to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` (single DC). The diff does not show any `|| "primary"` default for `events.update`, so this can result in `calendarId: undefined` and a failing Google update call when references provide no `externalCalendarId`.
